Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Right knee pain, associated with increased running and exercise; clicking present during activity.
- Pain onset ~2 weeks ago after starting longer training runs, worsened by running and some gym activities, alleviated by rest/ice.
- Occasional episode of knee swelling (early in course, resolved); no current swelling, redness, or warmth.
- No current limitation in range of motion; no locking, giving way, or instability.
- Occasional tingling in right toes noted briefly after exercise, not persistent.
- No similar symptoms in left knee; no symptoms in other joints or systemic features.
- Previous minor knee trauma (bruise) several months ago.
- Likely musculoskeletal/overuse etiology.
- Plan: Continue ice therapy; reduce running volume/intensity; physiotherapy referral for formal knee assessment recommended; consider imaging if symptoms persist or worsen; prescription for stronger anti-inflammatory agent (dose/route/frequency not documented) to be sent to pharmacy.
- Advised to seek urgent review if new or persistent swelling, heat, redness, high temperature, or inability to flex/extend knee develops.

Management Plan
- Continue use of ice therapy as needed.
- Reduce or modify running/training until assessed.
- Referral to physiotherapist for further assessment and management.
- Prescription for a stronger anti-inflammatory (dose/route/frequency not documented); not to be taken with current NSAIDs.
- Monitor for worsening or new concerning symptoms (e.g., persistent swelling, redness, fever, locked knee); seek urgent care if these occur.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
- Patellofemoral pain syndrome (Runner’s knee) – High likelihood. Supported by history of recent increased running, pain after activity, clicking, and normal examination other than pain provoked by exercise.
- Iliotibial band syndrome – Moderate likelihood. Right-sided/lateral knee pain, onset with increased running; some features less typical (site of pain and clicking).
- Meniscal injury (degenerative/minor tear) – Low likelihood. History of prior knee trauma and clicking, but no mechanical symptoms or recurrent swelling.
